questions.question: In which state/union territory is Losar celebrated to mark the start of the new year in that region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ladakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Losar** is the traditional **New Year festival** celebrated in the region of **Ladakh**.
 
• This festival marks the beginning of the **Tibetan Buddhist calendar year**.
 
• It is celebrated with great enthusiasm, involving **religious rituals, cultural performances, and social gatherings.**
 
• The festival usually takes place in **late December or early January**, depending on the lunar calendar.
 
• During Losar, people in Ladakh clean and decorate their homes, offer prayers, and perform traditional dances and music.
 
• Special dishes are prepared, including **Guthuk**, a traditional noodle soup.
 
• It is a time for **gratitude, renewal, and community bonding** in the cold and harsh winters of the region.
 
• Losar also holds spiritual significance as it involves rituals to drive away evil spirits and bring prosperity for the upcoming year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kerala**__

 __
 
• Kerala is known for its vibrant festivals, such as **Onam** and **Vishu**, but Losar is not celebrated here.
 
• **Onam** is a harvest festival celebrated in August or September and marks the return of the legendary king **Maveli**.
 
• **Vishu**, celebrated in April, marks the beginning of the Hindu New Year in Kerala.
 
 
 
• **Bihar**__
 __
 
• Bihar is known for festivals like **Chhath Puja** and **Sonepur Mela**, but Losar is not observed here.
 
• **Chhath Puja** is dedicated to the **Sun God** and involves rituals performed on riverbanks.
 
 
 
• **New Delhi**__
 
 
• New Delhi, as the capital of India, observes a mix of festivals from across the country, but Losar is not traditionally celebrated here.
 
• Being a cosmopolitan city, it hosts festivals like **Diwali, Eid, and Christmas** on a large scale.

questions.question: Kanak Rele, who established Nalanda Dance Research Centre, was a performer of which of the following classical dance forms of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohiniyattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kanak Rele** was a renowned performer, scholar, and researcher of the classical dance form **Mohiniyattam**, which originates from the Indian state of **Kerala**.
 
• She established the **Nalanda Dance Research Centre** in Mumbai, which is a pioneering institution for the study and promotion of Indian classical dance.
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is characterized by its **graceful movements**, soft expressions, and a unique blend of **music and rhythm**.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in the **Lasya style**, which emphasizes feminine grace and beauty.
 
• The themes of Mohiniyattam often revolve around **love and devotion**, particularly towards Lord Vishnu.
 
• Kanak Rele contributed significantly to the revival and academic study of Mohiniyattam, establishing it as a major classical dance form of India.
 
• Her work includes the publication of research and books that have enhanced the understanding and appreciation of **Mohiniyattam** globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Manipuri**__

 __
 
• **Manipuri** is a classical dance form originating from the northeastern Indian state of **Manipur**.
 
• This dance form is known for its **spiritual and devotional themes**, often depicting stories of **Radha and Krishna**.
 
• It features soft, graceful movements and is accompanied by traditional Manipuri music and instruments.
 
 
 
• **Kathak**__
 __
 
• **Kathak** is a classical dance form that originated in northern India.
 
• It is known for its **storytelling nature**, intricate footwork, and spins.
 
• The word "Kathak" comes from "Katha," meaning **story**, and the dance often narrates episodes from Hindu mythology.
 
• **Tabla and harmonium** are commonly used instruments in Kathak performances.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya**__
 
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form from the northeastern Indian state of **Assam**.
 
• It was introduced by the Vaishnavite saint **Sankardev** in the 15th century.
 
• This dance form is closely associated with the **Sattras**, the monasteries of Assam.
 
• Sattriya often depicts stories from the **Bhagavad Gita, Ramayana, and Mahabharata**.

questions.question: Which of the following acts introduced the system of dyarchy in the provincial administration in India?

options.text: The Government of India Act of 1909
The Government of India Act of 1919
The Government of India Act of 1935
The Government of India Act of 1947

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The Government of India Act of 1919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India Act of 1919** is also known as the **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**.
 
• This Act introduced the system of **dyarchy** in the provincial administration of India.
 
• **Dyarchy** refers to a dual system of governance where the provincial subjects were divided into two categories: **Reserved and Transferred subjects**.
 
• **Reserved subjects** (e.g., police, revenue, and justice) were under the control of the Governor and his Executive Council, responsible to the British government.
 
• **Transferred subjects** (e.g., agriculture, health, and education) were administered by Indian ministers who were responsible to the legislative council.
 
• The Act of 1919 aimed to gradually introduce **self-governing institutions** in India, as promised by the British government.
 
• This Act also expanded the **legislative councils** and introduced the concept of **direct elections** in India for the first time.
 
• The reforms were seen as a step towards **responsible government**, but they were criticized for limiting Indian participation and retaining significant British control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Government of India Act of 1909**__

 __
 
• Known as the **Morley-Minto Reforms**, this Act introduced the concept of **separate electorates** for Muslims in India.
 
• It aimed to increase Indian participation in the legislative councils by expanding their size and scope.
 
• The Act allowed for the indirect election of members to the Imperial Legislative Council.
 
• However, it did not introduce dyarchy or significant self-governance.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act of 1935**__
 __
 
• This Act introduced **provincial autonomy** and abolished the dyarchy system in the provinces.
 
• It proposed the establishment of an **All-India Federation**, which never materialized.
 
• The Act also introduced a bicameral legislature at the Centre and extended the franchise to more people.
 
• It is considered the longest and most detailed Act passed by the British Parliament concerning India.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act of 1947**__
 
 
• This Act, also known as the **Indian Independence Act**, marked the end of British rule in India.
 
• It partitioned British India into two independent dominions, **India and Pakistan**.
 
• The Act gave complete legislative sovereignty to the newly formed nations.
 
• It is regarded as the final legal framework for the independence of India.

questions.question: In which part of India is cool mountain climate observed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**North**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cool mountain climate** is primarily observed in the **northern part of India**, especially in the **Himalayan region**.
 
• The Himalayas are home to several locations with a **temperate climate**, characterized by **cool summers and cold winters**.
 
• Regions such as **Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim**, and parts of **Arunachal Pradesh** experience this climate.
 
• The elevation in the Himalayas plays a critical role in determining the temperature, with **higher altitudes** experiencing significantly cooler conditions.
 
• This climate type supports a unique **ecosystem**, with vegetation such as **coniferous forests** and alpine meadows.
 
• The cool mountain climate makes these regions popular for **tourism**, attracting visitors to destinations like **Shimla, Manali, Leh, and Darjeeling.**
 
• These areas are also vital for **glacial water resources**, which feed major rivers such as the **Ganga and Yamuna.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **West**__

 __
 
• The western part of India, including states like **Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Maharashtra**, experiences a **hot and arid climate** in regions like the Thar Desert.
 
• However, some parts, such as the **Western Ghats**, have a tropical climate with significant rainfall.
 
 
 
• **South**__
 __
 
• The southern region of India, particularly in states like **Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh**, has a **tropical climate** with warm temperatures and high humidity.
 
• The **Nilgiri Hills** in Tamil Nadu and Kerala experience a cooler climate but not as cold as the Himalayan region.
 
 
 
• **East**__
 
 
• The eastern part of India, including **West Bengal, Odisha, and Assam**, has a predominantly **humid subtropical climate** with high rainfall, especially during the monsoon season.
 
• Some parts of the northeast, like **Meghalaya**, are among the wettest places on Earth but do not experience the typical cool mountain climate of the north.

questions.question: Which of the following books is written by Dadabhai Naoroji?

options.text: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Poverty and Un-British Rule in India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji**, also known as the "Grand Old Man of India," was a prominent Indian political leader, economist, and social reformer.
 
• His book **Poverty and Un-British Rule in India** is a seminal work that discusses the economic exploitation of India under British colonial rule.
 
• The book introduced the concept of the **"Drain of Wealth"**, where he highlighted how the British transferred India's wealth to England.
 
• This book provides detailed analysis and data to show how colonial policies impoverished India while benefiting Britain.
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji's work played a critical role in raising awareness about the economic consequences of British rule among Indians and helped spark the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• He was the first Indian to be elected to the **British Parliament**, where he advocated for Indian rights and self-governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __
 
• This is not a book written by **Dadabhai Naoroji**. The title may appear similar but does not exist as an individual work.
 
 
 
• **Important Chapters of Poverty**__
 __
 
• This title is incorrect and does not correspond to any significant work in Indian economic or colonial literature.
 
 
 
• **Economics History of India**__
 
 
• While this title may sound plausible, it is not authored by **Dadabhai Naoroji**. It is likely confused with works by other economists and historians.

questions.question: The historical fiction 'The Glory of Patan' by KM Munshi was originally written in which Indian language?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• **'The Glory of Patan'** is part of the **Patan Trilogy**, a series of historical novels set in medieval Gujarat.
 
• The novel captures the essence of Gujarat's rich cultural heritage and the valor of the Chalukya dynasty, focusing on themes like heroism, loyalty, and the complexities of statecraft.
 
• It provides a vivid portrayal of the city of Patan, which was an important cultural and political center in Gujarat during the medieval period.
 
• The book reflects K. M. Munshi's deep understanding of India's history and his ability to weave it into compelling literary works.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The chemical compound present in turmeric is:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**curcumin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Curcumin** is the primary chemical compound found in **turmeric**, which is a spice derived from the root of the plant *Curcuma longa*.
 
• It is a **polyphenol** with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties.
 
• Curcumin has been extensively studied for its potential health benefits, such as improving symptoms of **arthritis, depression, and chronic diseases**.
 
• It contributes to the characteristic **yellow color** of turmeric and is commonly used as a natural food colorant.
 
• Curcumin is poorly absorbed in the bloodstream; hence, it is often consumed with **black pepper** (which contains piperine) to enhance its absorption.
 
• Turmeric is widely used in **Indian cuisine**, traditional medicine (like Ayurveda), and cosmetics.
 
• Research indicates that curcumin may have potential applications in treating conditions such as **heart diseases, Alzheimer's, and cancer**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tartaric Acid**__

 __
 
• **Tartaric acid** is an organic acid commonly found in fruits like **grapes, tamarinds, and bananas**.
 
• It is used in the food industry as a **preservative, acidulant, and stabilizer**, especially in baking.
 
• Tartaric acid plays a role in the production of **cream of tartar** and is also used in **winemaking** to control acidity.
 
 
 
• **Carotene**__
 __
 
• **Carotene** is a group of pigments found in plants that give them a **yellow, orange, or red** color.
 
• The most well-known type is **beta-carotene**, which is a precursor to **vitamin A** in the human body.
 
• Carotene is abundant in foods like **carrots, sweet potatoes, and spinach**.
 
• It is an important antioxidant and plays a vital role in maintaining **eye health and skin health**.
 
 
 
• **Capsaicin**__
 
 
• **Capsaicin** is the compound responsible for the **spicy heat** in chili peppers.
 
• It is widely used in **topical pain relief creams** due to its ability to desensitize nerve receptors.
 
• Capsaicin is also studied for its potential in **weight loss** and improving **metabolism**.
 
• It is used in **pepper sprays** as a self-defense tool.

questions.question: Who among the following established the Indore gharana?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ustad Amir Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ustad Amir Khan** was the founder of the **Indore Gharana** of Hindustani classical music.
 
• The Indore Gharana is known for its **slow and methodical elaboration** of ragas, focusing on the core essence of the raga.
 
• Ustad Amir Khan introduced the concept of **merging the styles** of Dhrupad and Khayal, creating a unique style of performance.
 
• He emphasized the use of **meend (glides between notes)** and the subtle ornamentation of notes to express the raga's mood.
 
• His renditions are characterized by **long alap (introductory improvisation)** and a serene, introspective approach.
 
• The Indore Gharana also incorporates the **bols (lyrics)** of the bandish in an innovative manner, adding emotional depth to the performance.
 
• **Ustad Amir Khan** was a highly influential figure in Indian classical music and inspired several musicians to adopt the Indore Gharana style.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhimsen Joshi**__

 __
 
• **Bhimsen Joshi** was a renowned vocalist of the **Kirana Gharana**, not the Indore Gharana.
 
• He is known for his powerful voice and mastery in **Khayal singing**.
 
• He was awarded the **Bharat Ratna** in 2008 for his contributions to Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Tansen**__
 __
 
• **Tansen** was one of the **Navaratnas** (nine gems) in the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar.
 
• He is considered the founder of the **Hindustani classical music tradition** but is not associated with the Indore Gharana.
 
• He is credited with composing several **ragas** like Miyan ki Todi and Miyan ki Malhar.
 
 
 
• **Ustad Ghaghe Khuda Baksh**__
 
 
• **Ustad Ghaghe Khuda Baksh** was an exponent of the **Gwalior Gharana**, the oldest Gharana of Hindustani classical music.
 
• He is not associated with the establishment of the Indore Gharana.
 
• The Gwalior Gharana is known for its focus on **pure and unembellished renditions** of ragas.

questions.question: The Rabi season of agriculture begins in October-November and ends in ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**March-April**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rabi season** is one of the two main agricultural seasons in India, the other being the **Kharif season**.
 
• The Rabi crops are sown during the **winter months**, typically in **October-November**.
 
• These crops are harvested in the spring season, which occurs around **March-April**.
 
• Rabi crops thrive in **cool weather** and require less water compared to Kharif crops.
 
• Examples of major Rabi crops include **wheat, barley, mustard, peas, and gram**.
 
• Rabi crops benefit from the **retreating monsoon moisture**, which helps in their growth during the winter months.
 
• Farmers ensure the crops are irrigated during this season as the winter months receive very little or no rainfall.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **June-July**__

 __
 
• The months of **June-July** mark the beginning of the **Kharif season**, not the Rabi season.
 
• This is the time when crops like **paddy, maize, and cotton** are sown, as these crops require more water and benefit from the **southwest monsoon rains**.
 
 
 
• **January-February**__
 __
 
• **January-February** falls in the middle of the Rabi cropping season and is primarily a **growth phase** for the crops rather than the harvest period.
 
 
 
• **May-June**__
 
 
• **May-June** is not associated with the Rabi season as it is the time when farmers begin preparing for the **Kharif season**.
 
• This period is characterized by **high temperatures** and the anticipation of the **onset of the monsoon**.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for sodium bicarbonate?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**NaHCO3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium bicarbonate**, commonly known as **baking soda**, has the chemical formula **NaHCO3**.
 
• It is classified as a **weak base** and is widely used in various applications such as **food preparation, cleaning, and pharmaceuticals**.
 
• It is a **white crystalline substance**, often appearing as a fine powder.
 
• The compound is made up of **sodium (Na), hydrogen (H), carbon (C), and oxygen (O)** atoms.
 
• It is used as a **leavening agent** in baking because it reacts with acids to release carbon dioxide, which causes dough or batter to rise.
 
• In medicine, it is used as an **antacid** to treat heartburn, indigestion, and upset stomach.
 
• It is also used in **fire extinguishers**, particularly for extinguishing grease fires.
 
• Sodium bicarbonate can neutralize acids, which makes it effective in cleaning and deodorizing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NaCl**__

 __
 
• **Sodium chloride (NaCl)**, commonly known as **table salt**, is used in food seasoning and preservation.
 
• It is composed of **sodium (Na) and chlorine (Cl)** ions.
 
• Sodium chloride is essential for maintaining **electrolyte balance** in the human body.
 
 
 
• **Na2CO3**__
 __
 
• **Sodium carbonate (Na2CO3)**, also called **washing soda**, is used in cleaning products and glass manufacturing.
 
• It is a strong base and is effective in **softening water** by removing calcium and magnesium ions.
 
• Sodium carbonate is widely used in the **textile and paper industries**.
 
 
 
• **NaOH**__
 
 
• **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**, also known as **caustic soda**, is a highly corrosive base.
 
• It is used in the manufacture of **soap, paper, and various chemicals**.
 
• Sodium hydroxide is commonly used in laboratories for **neutralizing acids**.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the features of capital goods?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**They are durable.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Capital goods** are physical assets used by companies to produce goods and services. They include machinery, tools, buildings, and equipment.
 
• A key characteristic of capital goods is that they are **durable**. This means they are designed for long-term use and do not get consumed in a single production cycle.
 
• Capital goods assist in the production of **consumer goods** but are not the final goods themselves.
 
• Examples include **industrial machinery, tools, vehicles used in factories, and infrastructure facilities**.
 
• The durability of capital goods helps businesses generate revenue over an extended period, making them a critical component of **economic growth and industrial development**.
 
• Their durability also means they require regular **maintenance** to remain functional and efficient.
 
• In economic terms, capital goods are considered part of **fixed assets**, contributing significantly to the production process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **They are inexpensive**__

 __
 
• Capital goods are generally **expensive** due to their specialized nature and durability. Examples like **industrial machinery** or **factory equipment** involve substantial investment.
 
• The high cost reflects their ability to generate returns over a long period, which is why they are not classified as inexpensive.
 
 
 
• **They are Giffen goods**__
 __
 
• **Giffen goods** are a unique category in economics where demand for a product increases as its price rises, contrary to the law of demand. Examples include certain staple goods like **bread or rice** in extreme poverty scenarios.
 
• Capital goods are not Giffen goods because their demand does not follow this principle; it depends on industrial requirements and economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **They are inferior goods**__
 
 
• **Inferior goods** are those for which demand decreases as consumer incomes rise, such as **low-cost substitutes** like public transportation over private vehicles.
 
• Capital goods are not inferior goods, as they are essential for production and are independent of income levels.

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties established the Vijayanagara kingdom in fourteenth century?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sangama dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sangama dynasty** was the founding dynasty of the **Vijayanagara Empire**, established in the **14th century**.
 
• The empire was founded in **1336 CE** by two brothers, **Harihara I** and **Bukka Raya I**, who were previously commanders under the Hoysala Empire.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire played a crucial role in the preservation of **Hindu culture and traditions** during a time of Islamic invasions in South India.
 
• The Sangama dynasty ruled until the mid-15th century, when it was succeeded by the **Saluva dynasty**.
 
• The empire's capital, **Vijayanagara**, was located near the modern-day city of **Hampi in Karnataka**, which is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire contributed significantly to **art, architecture, and literature**, including the construction of iconic monuments like the **Virupaksha Temple**.
 
• The Sangama dynasty's rule marked the beginning of the empire's development as a major power in South India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aravidu dynasty**__

 __
 
• The **Aravidu dynasty** was the fourth and final dynasty to rule the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• It was established in the late **16th century** by **Aliya Rama Raya**, following the decline of the Tuluva dynasty.
 
• This dynasty saw the empire's eventual decline after the **Battle of Talikota** (1565), which led to the fall of Vijayanagara.
 
 
 
• **Saluva dynasty**__
 __
 
• The **Saluva dynasty** succeeded the Sangama dynasty in the late **15th century**.
 
• It was founded by **Saluva Narasimha Deva Raya**, who rose to power during a period of political instability.
 
• This dynasty laid the groundwork for the eventual rise of the Tuluva dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Tuluva dynasty**__
 
 
• The **Tuluva dynasty** was the third dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire and is often considered its **golden age**.
 
• It was founded by **Veeranarasimha Raya** and reached its zenith under **Krishnadevaraya**, one of the most celebrated rulers of the empire.
 
• Krishnadevaraya expanded the empire and promoted advancements in **art, architecture, and literature**.

questions.question: The red colour of tomatoes is due to the presence of:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**lycopene**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lycopene** is a natural red pigment responsible for the **red colour of tomatoes**.
 
• It is a type of **carotenoid**, which is a class of pigments found in plants that play a role in photosynthesis and provide various colours to fruits and vegetables.
 
• Lycopene is a powerful **antioxidant**, which helps in neutralizing free radicals in the body and reducing oxidative stress.
 
• It is highly concentrated in **tomatoes**, but it is also found in other red fruits and vegetables like **watermelon, red bell peppers, papaya, and pink grapefruit.**
 
• Lycopene is known for its potential **health benefits**, such as reducing the risk of certain types of cancers (like prostate cancer) and improving heart health.
 
• Its bioavailability increases when tomatoes are cooked or processed into products like **tomato paste, sauce, or juice.**
 
• Lycopene is lipophilic, meaning it is better absorbed by the body when consumed with a source of **fat.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Limonene**__

 __
 
• **Limonene** is a natural compound found in the peels of citrus fruits like oranges and lemons.
 
• It is commonly used in **cleaning products, food flavorings, and perfumes** due to its strong citrus scent.
 
• Limonene has potential health benefits, including **anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties.**
 
• It is not responsible for the red colour in tomatoes.
 
 
 
• **Beta carotene**__
 __
 
• **Beta carotene** is an orange-red pigment found in many fruits and vegetables, such as **carrots, sweet potatoes, and pumpkins.**
 
• It is a precursor to **vitamin A**, essential for vision, skin health, and immune function.
 
• While beta carotene contributes to the orange colour of some foods, it is not the pigment responsible for the red colour in tomatoes.
 
 
 
• **Alizarin**__
 
 
• **Alizarin** is an organic compound historically used as a **red dye in textiles.**
 
• It is derived from the root of the **madder plant.**
 
• Alizarin is not related to the pigmentation of fruits or vegetables and has no connection to tomatoes.

questions.question: With which sport is Sanjana Bathula associated?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Roller Skating**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sanjana Bathula** is a renowned sportsperson associated with **Roller Skating**.
 
• Roller Skating is a sport that involves moving on surfaces with the help of **specialized shoes fitted with rollers or wheels**.
 
• This sport requires a high level of **balance, coordination, agility, and speed**.
 
• **Sanjana Bathula** has represented India at several **national and international roller skating competitions** and has earned recognition for her skills.
 
• Roller skating is widely practiced for both **recreational and competitive purposes**.
 
• It is included in various events such as **speed skating, artistic skating, and roller hockey.**
 
• Roller Skating has become increasingly popular among youths, particularly in countries like **India, the USA, and China.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Squash**__

 __
 
• Squash is a **racquet sport** played between two players (singles) or four players (doubles) in a four-walled court.
 
• The players alternate in hitting a small, hollow rubber ball against the front wall.
 
• It is popular in countries like **England, Egypt, and the USA**.
 
• Unlike roller skating, squash emphasizes **hand-eye coordination, speed, and endurance.**
 
 
 
• **Shooting**__
 __
 
• Shooting is a sport that involves **precision and accuracy** in aiming and hitting a target using firearms or air guns.
 
• This sport is divided into various categories such as **rifle shooting, pistol shooting, and trap/skeet shooting.**
 
• It is a popular event in the **Olympics** and other international competitions.
 
• Shooting requires **concentration, focus, and control**, unlike the physical agility needed in roller skating.
 
 
 
• **Badminton**__
 
 
• Badminton is a popular **racquet sport** played using a shuttlecock and racquets, usually between two or four players.
 
• The game is played on a **rectangular court** divided by a net.
 
• It emphasizes **speed, reflexes, and stamina** and is especially popular in **Asian countries like China, India, and Indonesia.**
 
• Prominent Indian players like **P.V. Sindhu and Saina Nehwal** have gained international fame in Badminton.

questions.question: Who was the captain of Royal Challengers Bangalore in the Women's Premier League event 2023?

• She was appointed as the **captain** of the **Royal Challengers Bangalore (RCB)** team in the inaugural **Women's Premier League (WPL) 2023**.
 
• Mandhana is recognized as one of the most talented batters in women's cricket and has represented India in **international cricket** across all formats.
 
• She holds the distinction of being the first Indian woman cricketer to score a **double century in a one-day game**, achieving this milestone in domestic cricket.
 
• Smriti Mandhana was also awarded the prestigious **ICC Women's Cricketer of the Year** in **2018**.
 
• Her leadership and batting prowess have been pivotal in shaping the RCB team's strategy and performance during the WPL 2023.
 
• Mandhana’s appointment as captain reflects her **experience, consistency, and ability to inspire the team.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __
 
• **Harmanpreet Kaur** is an Indian cricketer who serves as the captain of the Indian women's cricket team.
 
• She led the **Mumbai Indians** in the Women's Premier League (WPL) 2023, not Royal Challengers Bangalore.
 
• Harmanpreet is known for her aggressive batting style and has played a crucial role in several high-pressure matches for India.
 
 
 
• **Deepti Sharma**__
 __
 
• **Deepti Sharma** is an Indian all-rounder known for her contributions with both bat and ball.
 
• She played for the **UP Warriorz** team in the Women's Premier League 2023.
 
• Deepti has a reputation for her versatility and is an integral part of the Indian women's cricket team.
 
 
 
• **Shafali Verma**__
 
 
• **Shafali Verma** is a young and dynamic Indian cricketer known for her explosive batting.
 
• She captained the **Delhi Capitals** team in the Women's Premier League 2023.
 
• Shafali is celebrated for her fearless batting approach and has gained recognition as one of the brightest talents in women's cricket.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the famous place Mawsynram?

A. It is the wettest place on the earth.

B. It is located in Meghalaya state of India.

options.text: Neither A nor B is correct.
A and B both are correct.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A and B both are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mawsynram** is recognized as the **wettest place on Earth**, receiving the highest annual rainfall.
 
• It is located in the **East Khasi Hills district** of the state of **Meghalaya**, India.
 
• The average annual rainfall in Mawsynram is around **11,871 mm**, making it globally renowned for its heavy precipitation.
 
• The region's extreme rainfall is due to its location on the southern slopes of the **Khasi Hills**, which intercept the moist monsoon winds from the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Mawsynram's environment is characterized by **lush green landscapes**, dense vegetation, and unique biodiversity due to the continuous rainfall.
 
• The nearby village of **Cherrapunji** (also located in Meghalaya) previously held the record for the wettest place on Earth but has since been surpassed by Mawsynram.
 
• Meghalaya, also known as the "Abode of Clouds," is famous for its **picturesque scenery**, **living root bridges**, and **caves**.
 
• Mawsynram's climate and geography make it a significant site for **meteorological studies** and attract tourists seeking to explore its unique natural beauty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Only A is correct**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because it ignores the **specific location** of Mawsynram in the state of Meghalaya, India.
 
 
 
• **Neither A nor B is correct**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect as both statements (A and B) are factually accurate regarding **Mawsynram** being the wettest place on Earth and its location in **Meghalaya**.
 
 
 
• **Only B is correct**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect because it disregards the fact that Mawsynram is indeed recognized as the **wettest place on Earth**.

questions.question: How many countries share their land borders with India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Seven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **India shares its land borders with seven countries**, namely **Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and Afghanistan.**
 
• The **longest border** that India shares is with **Bangladesh (4,096 km).**
 
• The shortest border is with **Afghanistan, which spans only 106 km** in the Wakhan Corridor region.
 
• The India-China border is referred to as the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**, and it is approximately 3,488 km long.
 
• The border between India and Pakistan is known as the **Radcliffe Line**, which was drawn during the partition of India in **1947.**
 
• The India-Nepal border is an **open border**, allowing free movement of people between the two countries without a visa.
 
• The **India-Bhutan border** is 699 km long and serves as an important route for trade and cultural exchange.
 
• The **India-Myanmar border**, spanning 1,643 km, is strategically crucial due to its location in the northeastern region and its role in trade and connectivity with Southeast Asia.
